newsitem.title: UK: West African crude tanker rates seen falling.
newsitem.headline: West African crude tanker rates seen falling.

text.p: The West African crude tanker market looks set to fall as the U.S. shows a preference for Middle Eastern cargoes, brokers said on Friday.
"There's a lot of Arab crude going to the U.S. with freight rates down from the (Middle East) Gulf.
"Demand from West Africa is falling as a result," one broker said.

Rates for 130,000 tonnes from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf/USAC were currently put at W82.5 and W85 for the Knock Sheen and London Splendour, both for Sun, but the broker said rates were likely to fall next week.
From the Gulf to South Korea, W62 was seen for the 1992-built Irian for Ssangyong, which brokers said was typical for a new vessel and reflected Korean insistence on modern tonnage.
In the transatlantic sector, the Nisyros was seen fixed at W80 for 134,000 tonnes for Koch from Hound Point to the U.S. Gulf.
The Kamlesh was seen fixed with 130,000 tonnes from Norway to the Med at about W95 for Statoil, while in the Western Hemisphere, Caribs/USAC was fixed around W195 for 50,000 tonnes.
A few fuel oil fixings were also seen, including the Talava with 25,000 tonnes on a Cont/UKC trip at W185. The charterer was not reported.

Asian fixtures were relatively sparse, but included two 80,000 tonners, the Bering Sea from Pulau Sambu to South Korea at W132.5 for LG and the Loul'wat Qatar from Dampier to Singapore at W130 for Mobil.
